description: Exercise C-verify-current-authority with four live nodes and an actual partition. The old leader remains with a nonvoter while the two other voters elect and commit. Distinguish old-authority VerifyLeader success from lease/error protection after accounting for pre-partition reply paths. Preparation and raw RPC events are diagnostics; only the admitted future result is compared.

harness.description: TestAssuranceVerifyAfterCompetingCommit; four live NewRaft instances, normal public membership/election/apply/verification paths, supported in-memory stores and non-pipelined transport wrapper.
semantic_changes: No target source or dependency changes.
Transport wrapper returns partition errors across a,n versus b,c and returns ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported; real successful responses pass through unchanged.
Driver logs actual RPCs and synchronized observations; all prerequisites are checked before their events are emitted.

legality.derivation: Fresh NewRaft nodes use injected in-memory stores and transport with no persistence failures. Bootstrap only a as sole voter, then complete AddVoter(b), AddVoter(c), AddNonvoter(n), and a command applied on every peer. Each actual configuration is read and suffrage checked before a fixed partition. The wrapper changes only delivery policy: calls hold a shared network read lock, partition takes the write lock, and cross-partition RPCs thereafter return errors. Only AppendEntriesPipeline is unsupported, using the existing ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported contract. The two serial sender paths per old-leader voter must each begin a new blocked call after the partition; by their source loops this follows processing of any preceding pre-partition reply. No pipeline, snapshot or configuration work overlaps verification. Real votes, successful Apply and matching higher-term stored command copies on b and c establish the competing authority before a.VerifyLeader. API futures are awaited once in a helper goroutine; matching channel receipt synchronizes the subsequent Index read. MockFSM content is read under its own mutex; stored logs are obtained by the store read API. Shutdown is invoked on all nodes after the observation window, then each Shutdown future is awaited and transports closed. No conclusion is drawn from cleanup state.
legality.applicability: a and n use heartbeat/election/lease 1500ms; b and c use 50ms; all use CommitTimeout 5ms and real timers. Config validates every peer. No claim of a protocol response deadline is made from the 3-second observation cap.
unresolved: This schedule exercises a supported non-pipelined in-memory transport and asymmetric server-local timers, not every transport or timer configuration.
No external client read endpoint is simulated. FSM divergence is diagnostic; the principal observation is the VerifyLeader result after independently completed competing commitment.

grounding.derivation: The result event is emitted only after the same VerifyLeader future Error() returns. success is computed as err == nil. It is separate from the pre-invocation admission event. The correlated competing prerequisite records actual higher-term log copies and applied command on both majority voters. For this established obsolete authority, a successful return contradicts C-verify-current-authority. Missing result or setup failure is unknown, not false success.
grounding.applicability: One fixed scenario and operation identity; future completion precedes result emission. No filtering on success, old_role or old_has_new_command.
unresolved: This finite check can witness an improper success or a completed error; it cannot prove eventual completion when the result is missing.

observable_properties.description: For the verification admitted after the higher-term competing commitment under the retained partition, its completed future must report an error rather than success.

uncertainties: Execution must actually attain all declared prefix prerequisites; source plausibility does not establish them.
Raw response and blocked-path events must be reviewed against the two serial sender loops before attributing any failure specifically to nonvoter counting.
